question.leadin: Identify some of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: King Nebuchadnezzar ("NEB-uh-kud-NEZZ-ur") of Chaldea ("cal-DEE-uh") built these structures for his wife Amytis ("AM-uh-tis") of Media. They consisted of terraces and irrigation structures that serviced a variety of luscious trees.
question.clue: According to Strabo, an early version of Archimedes' Screw was built for use at this location.

swap.text: Babylonia, a successor state in Mesopotamia, was ruled for a time by this man, whose law code mentioned an "eye for an eye," and is the world's oldest known law code.
swap.clue: This Amorite king went up a mountain to receive a stele from the sun god Shamash that was later discovered in Susa.

question.text: The Sumerians invented textbooks while teaching scribes this Mesopotamian writing system at the eduba. This writing system was designed for reeds to be pressed into clay tablets.
question.clue: Henry Rawlinson studied the Behistun Inscription for insight into this system, which is seen on the oldest complaint tablet.

swap.text: The Code of Hammurabi was issued from this ancient city on the Euphrates[yoo-FRAY-teez]River.
swap.clue: After the Battle of Opis, the Achaemenids were able to capture this city by diverting the Euphrates river to make it more shallow.

question.leadin: Amar-Sin (AA-mar-sin), Shu-Sin (SHOO-sin), and Ibbi-Sin (IB-ee-sin) all succeeded a reformer of this city's Third Dynasty named Shulgi (SHOOL-ghee).
question.text: Name this city near the mouth of the Euphrates (yoo-FRAY-teez), whose Great Ziggurat (ZIG-uh-raht) was later restored by King Nabonidus (NAA-boh-NAI-dus).
question.answerHtml: Ur [or Urim; or Uru; do not accept or prompt on “Uruk”]
question.clue: A king named -Nammu, who founded a dynasty that supplanted Lagash and the Gutians, was succeeded by Shulgi.

swap.text: This Neo-Assyrian ruler's destructive conquest of Elam is sometimes considered genocide. This ruler's namesake library, discovered by Austen Henry Layard, contained the Epic of Gilgamesh.
swap.clue: This ruler had to replace the king of Babylon after his brother Shamash-shum-ukin revolted.

question.leadin: This empire fell to the Medes and the Babylonians in the 610 B.C. fall of Harran.
question.text: Name this empire, whose capitals included Assur ("ASS-er") and Nineveh. Tiglath-Pileser III instituted numerous reforms in this empire.
question.clue: This empire's final defeat came when Harran fell, an act precipitated by the civil war that broke out between Sin-shar-ishkun and Ashur-etel-ilani.

swap.text: This Assyrian capital was located on the northern part of the Tigris.
swap.clue: This city was sacked by a coalition including Scythians assembled in 612 BC by the Median king Cyaxares ("kye-ax-AIR-ees"), ending the dominance of a line that included Tiglath-Pileser III.

question.leadin: Although not Moses, one story about this ruler's birth sees his high priestess mother put him into a basket to flow down a river eventually to Ishtar.
question.text: Name this father of Enheduanna, Rimush, Manishtushu who conquered Uruk from Lugal-Zage-Si and eventually all of Sumeria. He also conquered up to the Cedar Forest, or modern day Lebanon. His empire fell within 100 years of his death after Zagros barbarians called the Gutians invaded.
question.answerHtml: Sargon the Great [accept Sargon of Akkad; Note: do not say 2nd answer if they don’t answer with that answer]
question.clue: He appointed his daughter Enheduanna high priestess, and his empire reached its greatest expanse under his grandson Naram-sin.

swap.leadin: The largest remains of one of these structures can be found at Chonga Zanbil, which was built by the Elamites.
swap.text: Name these terraced religious buildings. A seven-storied example called the Etemenanki, which was dedicated to the god Marduk, got a reference in Herodotus's histories.
swap.clue: Koldewey also found one that he took to be a temple to Marduk, the name of which, Etemenanki, translates as "The Foundation of Heaven and Earth."

question.text: Gilgamesh was the fifth king of this Sumerian city, which was founded by Enmerkar.
question.clue: The Ubaid period preceded this city's namesake "Protoliterate" period.

swap.leadin: Identify these peoples of the Ancient Near East.
swap.text: This Mesopotamian tribe, with capital at Wassukkani in modern-day Syria, was powerful from 1510-1360 BCE, especially under King Saustatar.
swap.clue: Based on terms in the Kikkuli horse-training manual, the names of several rulers, and a list of deities found in a treaty, the rulers of this polity are argued to have been Indo-Europeans.

question.text: While conducting excavations in Assyria, Layard found many of these statues of winged human headed bulls, which were often found in pairs at the entrances of buildings. Their male counterparts are called shedu.
question.clue: Several Mesopotamian empires, but most notably the Assyrians, built statues of these protective creatures with a person's face, eagle's wings, and the body of either a bull or a lion.

swap.leadin: Invading Egypt sure can get messy.
swap.text: According to Herodotus, the invasion of Egypt by this empire's king Sennacherib was stymied when mice ate the bowstrings of his army. This empire with capital at Nineveh was later ruled by Ashurbanipal.
swap.clue: A king of this empire built an elaborate palace at Khorsabad called Dur-Sharrukin, whose gate included carvings of winged bulls with human-faces called lamassu.

question.leadin: Objects such as an axe with a copper and gold handle adorned with a boar attest to the influence of these people's culture in Ugarit.
question.text: Name these people whose namesake language was primarily spoken in the Mitanni kingdom.
question.clue: This ethnic group largely made up the population of the Mitanni Kingdom to the southeast of the Hittite Empire. Kikkuli ("kee-KOO-lee") wrote a horse training manual in this ethnic group's namesake language, which was most closely related to Urartian.

swap.leadin: This ruler is the main character of the Cutha Legend and The Great Revolt, which may have inspired later legends to blame him for Akkad's conquest by the Gutians.
swap.text: Name this ruler of the Akkadian Empire during its territorial peak and the first to proclaim his own divinity. This ruler's namesake "Victory Stele" depicts his victory over the Lullubi people.
swap.clue: This king who ruled during the height of the Akkadian Empire, and erected a notable victory stele boasting of his defeat of the mountain people of Lullubi and depicting himself as a god.

question.text: Several Chaldaean leaders, including Marduk-apla-usur and Eriba-Marduk, ruled over this kingdom in the 8th century B.C. Nebuchadnezzar II ruled during the "Chaldean dynasty" of a "Neo-" empire of this kingdom.
question.clue: A raid from its western neighbors left it in the hands of the Kassites, and part of it was destroyed by Sennacherib but later rebuilt by his son Essarhadon.

swap.leadin: King Shulgi of Ur built a 150 mile wall to defend against these people.
swap.text: Name this Semitic people who established the cities of Ebla and Mari while usurping cities like Kish and Eshnunna. The most famous member of this people conquered Larsa from Rim-Sin I and also instituted a draconian law code demanding "an eye for an eye."
swap.answerHtml: Amorites [or Martu; or Amurru; prompt on but DO NOT OTHERWISE MENTION Babylonians]
swap.clue: Larsa attained independence from Isin under the governor Gungunum, who was of this ethnicity. Hammurabi belonged to this ethnicity, whose members ruled Babylon before the Kassites and Elamites.

question.leadin: Daniel Fleming discussed "early collective governance" in this polity, which was mostly comprised of Sim'alite and Yaminite tribal confederations.
question.text: Name this polity founded in the early Bronze Age, a major rival of Ebla. "Terrestrial" and "celestial" domains are delineated in a painting from this polity showing a ruler's "investiture."
question.answerHtml: Mari [accept Tell Hariri] (The painting is the investiture of Zimri-Lim.)
question.clue: While providing terminology for parts of the body, animals, and economic functions, the names of specific people are largely absent from a peace treaty between this city and Ebla.

swap.leadin: The only woman attested to in this document is Kug-Bu, the Tavern Keeper.
swap.text: Name this compendium of rulers that includes five dynasties of Kish and three dynasties of Ur.
